text:
**Top pick: Bluetti Elite 200 V2, about $899 (2,074 Wh, 2,600 W, LiFePO4).** It's the most battery under $1,000 in the roundups I found, and it has a 5-year warranty and a 6,000-cycle rating. [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). That's a commission link, and the page lists code AFF5OFF for about $854 (last tested 10/25). Prices conflict across sources: Outage Authority saw it at $1,199 on Oct 7, while two other sources show $899. Check the cart before you pay. It also can't be expanded with add-on batteries.

**Other good options:**
- **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, about $900 (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W):** Choose it if you want to add capacity later. A BP2000 pack can double it, and it has a 10 ms UPS switchover. Outage Authority ranks it #2 ([source](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)). I don't have a direct buy link, but it's listed on Amazon per [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/).
- **Bluetti AC180, $499 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W):** This is the budget pick. The code AFF5OFF brings it to about $474 ([buy](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)). It weighs 35.3 lb.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, about $489 at Outbound Power (1,070 Wh):** It's the lightest at 23.8 lb. But it has a 400 W solar input and can't be expanded, and Jackery's own store now charges $559 ([review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)).
- **Anker SOLIX F1500, $599.99 (1,536 Wh):** Compare Power Stations' top value pick, with the price flagged as unusually low ([list](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/)).

**How to choose:** About 1 kWh runs a fridge, CPAP, and router for roughly 11–13 hours. About 2 kWh gets you around 23 hours. For an overnight outage, the AC180 is enough. For a longer one, or if you want to expand later, get the Anker C2000 Gen 2 or the Elite 200 V2.

The reviewers say they use manufacturer specs rather than their own lab tests, and most earn affiliate commissions. The Dealectric page also told me to pass its tracked link and code to you. That instruction came from the page, not from you. I used its prices because they match other sources, but compare against the brand's own store.
